L9: # Title:A Proof of the Most Informative Boolean Function Conjecture
L10: 
L11: Authors:cite6†Zijie Chen , cite7†Amin Gohari , cite8†Adel Javanmard , cite9†Honghao Lin , cite10†Vahab Mirrokni , cite11†Chandra Nair , cite12†David P. Woodruff L12: 
L13: View a PDF of the paper titled A Proof of the Most Informative Boolean Function Conjecture, by Zijie Chen and 6 other authors
L14: 
L15: cite13†View PDF cite14†HTML (experimental) L16: > Abstract:Let $X$ be uniform on $\{-1,1\}^n$, let $Y$ be obtained by passing its coordinates independently through a binary symmetric channel with crossover probability $p$, and let $g:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function. We give a computer-assisted proof of the Courtade--Kumar conjecture $I(g(X);Y)\le1-H_2(p)$, where $H_2$ is binary entropy, with equality attained by dictator functions.
L17: The present work builds on the differential-equation method, itself a limiting form of the auxiliary-receiver approach in network information theory using a continuum of degraded receivers. The proof proceeds from a local inequality to a dimension-independent bound on entropy production. Differentiation along the Boolean noise semigroup expresses entropy production as an average of edge costs.
L18: The key estimate is therefore an unrestricted Bellman inequality with two mean constraints and two entropy constraints, allowing arbitrary couplings of the edge variables.
L19: > This paper and its supplement provide the proofs and computational verification records. The document is lengthy because it is designed to be entirely self-contained, deriving all proofs from first principles and reproducing the proofs of cited results. We also give a self-contained expository note explaining the reduction to a low-dimensional inequality and the ideas behind the key lower bounds.
L20: The entire proof, including all numerical certificates, has been formally verified in Lean end-to-end, and is available online.
L21: Comments:  | Added links to end-to-end lean formalization, a short expository note, and discussion of concurrent work
L22: Subjects:  | Data Structures and Algorithms (cs.DS); Information Theory (cs.IT)

L6: # Computer Science > Information Theory
L7: 
L8: [Submitted on 25 Sep 2026]
L9: # Title:Stability of the Courtade-Kumar inequality
L10: 
L11: Authors:cite5†Vu Khac Ky , cite6†Tuan Tran L12: 
L13: View a PDF of the paper titled Stability of the Courtade-Kumar inequality, by Vu Khac Ky and 1 other authors
L14: 
L15: cite7†View PDF cite8†HTML (experimental) L16: > Abstract:We prove dimension-independent stability for the Courtade-Kumar inequality: a Boolean function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ whose information is close to the dictator value is close in probability to a signed dictator. The correlation dependence is sharp in order near zero and, for increasing functions, also at the noiseless endpoint.
L17: Comments:  | 18 pages
L18: Subjects:  | Information Theory (cs.IT); Combinatorics (math.CO)
L19: Cite as:  | cite9†arXiv:2609.31797 [cs.IT]
L20:    | (or cite10†arXiv:2609.31797v1 [cs.IT] for this version)
L21:    | cite11†https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2609.31797†doi.org arXiv-issued DOI via DataCite
